headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud takes [[6 for 55 to bowl out Australia]] for 198
headline: Hasan Mahmud takes 6 for 55 to bowl out Australia for 198
summary: The pacer's career-best figures helped Bangladesh secure a strong start in their first Test series in Australia in 23 years.
details: Hasan Mahmud delivered a dream opening day at the Marrara Stadium, claiming a career-best six wickets for 55 runs. His performance helped Bangladesh bowl out a formidable Australian side for 198 on the first day of the Test.

Much of the buildup to the series had focused on Nahid Rana's express pace, but Hasan filled the void through movement, control, and intelligent planning. He used his experience from the County Championship with Kent to adapt to the conditions.

Hasan's success was built on deliberate planning with team analysts. He varied his bowling side and used the crease to create chances, specifically targeting batters like Travis Head and Jake Weatherald.

The pitch proved to be slightly tacky due to dew, providing enough assistance for the Bangladesh quicks. Taskin Ahmed and Hasan set the tone in the opening session, putting the Australian batters under immediate pressure.

This dominant start marks a memorable beginning to Bangladesh's first Test series in Australia in over two decades. Hasan's guile and execution proved that the Tigers have more to offer than just sheer speed.

headline: 5 workers die from suspected toxic gas at Sitakunda shipyard
summary: The victims were dismantling an LNG carrier at Ferdous Steel Shipyard in the Bhatiary area when the incident occurred.
details: Five workers died after being exposed to suspected toxic gas inside a ship being dismantled at a shipbreaking yard in Sitakunda’s Bhatiary area today.
Firefighters recovered the bodies from the vessel in the sea adjacent to Ferdous Steel Shipyard in the morning.
Six people were brought to Chattogram Medical College Hospital, where five were declared dead by doctors and one remains admitted for treatment.
The shipyard manager, Mohammad Yusuf, stated that an LNG carrier was being dismantled and cutting work was nearly complete when the accident happened.
He added that liquid waste was found in a section of the vessel, and the tragedy occurred when a safety officer and others went to inspect it.
The Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments (DIFE) is currently working to determine the exact cause of the accident.
